entries.title: generate the diagnostic index and the command-line reference
entries.body:
The reference now covers the compiler itself, under a new Compiler reference group. Diagnostics lists every `NL` code `--json` can print, grouped by band. Each code has its anchor (`#nl2387`), its rule text, and the programs from `tests/wordings/` that provoke it, with their exact output. Command line lists every flag `nish --help` prints, read from the help table itself, so the page and the help cannot drift apart. The guide's CLI page links both.

`scripts/gen-reference.mjs` reads `src/codes.ts` and `src/cli-style.ts` with the TypeScript parser, and never by running the compiler. It fails the run in four cases: the page's code count differs from `RULE_COUNT` plus the four band-0 codes, an example lacks its `.err`, a help statement or argument has a shape it cannot read, or a table is not where it expects it. `--check` reports either page as stale when its sources change.

entries.title: plan WP49 stage 5 and bring the WP49 plan statuses up to date
entries.body: Stage 5 splits into four pull requests: the executor (runtime-async.c, nish:async readable, writable and sleep, a slab per spawned kind, a region per task), async fetch with an eager body under a cap, serve with the async Postgres pool, and cancellation. The WP49 plan now marks the renames, Upstream and the carrier, the TFB database tests, regions and the async language as done, and points its executor section at the new plan.

entries.title: measure Http1Server CPU per request end to end, 0.34.1 vs 0.35.0
entries.body:
bench/http1-e2e runs the multicore-server-challenge submission under the
challenge's own loadgen (15,000 users, 60 s ramp, 120 s measure) and
measures the HTTP workers' CPU per request in alternating rounds: A is
0.34.1, B is 0.35.0 with the same source, C is 0.35.0 with sendBody.
aarch64 figures come from hardware counters; the x86 VM, which has no
PMU, uses schedstat, cachegrind and a tracefs syscall trace.

Neither 0.35.0 arm saves CPU beyond one arm's own spread (aarch64 A
14,410 ns, B +9, C +32, spread 414-636; x86 A 17,818 ns, B +265,
C +304, spread 638-1,179). Kernel time is 56-70% of the workers' CPU.
The library stages worth cutting are Jwt.verify's HMAC-SHA256 (~2.9 us
on x86), the http1 head parse (~1-1.25 us) and the JSON tokenizer
(~0.47 us). None of the four socket knobs tried moved beyond the noise.

Measured: aarch64 5 rounds per arm, x86 4 rounds per arm; same-arm spread 414-1,179 ns/request
Refs: bench/http1-e2e/README.md
Part of #1275
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: document or internalise std/net's undocumented public fields
entries.body:
Every public field in std/net's QUIC, TLS and HTTP modules now carries a doc comment, so the library reference describes what each one holds, its unit or range, and why a caller reads it. Before this change, 283 of those fields had no doc. Nine fields that only other std modules read are tagged `@internal` instead, which removes them from the reference. Each of those nine names its reader. Any field that a test, an example or a doc page reads gets a real comment.

The `@param` and `@returns` of `PgConnection.paramTextArray` now parse. A backslash inside a code span had been escaping the closing backtick, which swallowed both tags.

Only comments and `@internal` tags change. Every changed std file has the same comment-free AST as before, and the regenerated goldens move only by source line numbers.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: fail gen-reference --check on an undocumented public declaration
entries.body:
`node scripts/gen-reference.mjs --check`, which CI already runs, now fails when a public declaration in std/ or runtime/nish.d.ts lacks documentation. A declaration needs a doc comment, a `@param` for each parameter, and a `@returns` for any return type other than void or never. TypeDoc's notDocumented validation covers functions, classes, interfaces, constructors, methods, properties, accessors, variables, type aliases, enums and enum members. It checks the same reflections the reference pages are built from, so `@internal` and private members are excluded, and it skips members inherited from TypeScript's lib. A second pass of the script's own checks `@param` and `@returns` on functions, methods, constructors, accessors and call signatures.

Today's gaps live in scripts/undocumented.txt, one `module.Name.member` per line. The list only shrinks. `--check` fails on a gap the file does not list, and on a listed line that is no longer a gap. `--update-baseline` refuses to add a line, and only `--grow-baseline` adds one, for a change to the rule itself. The list holds 2 entries, the `HostHandle` brand member, down from 299 measured before this work. This change also documents the missing `@param` tags in runtime/nish.d.ts and `ResultErr.ok`.

The rule is written down in .claude/comments.md, CLAUDE.md's definition of done, and docs/README.md's "The library reference". src/ is out of scope, because the compiler's exports are not a user API.

entries.title: let a spec-first module's emitted test sit in test/spec/
entries.body:
A std module can land spec-first: one PR adds its spec, the contract that
quotes it and the Nish test vector emits from it, and a second adds the
module. The emitted test lives in test/spec/, a path vector's frozen gate
fixes, and imports a module that does not exist until the second PR, so knip
reported it as an unused file and failed lint:dead. Knip now takes
test/spec/*.ts as entries, and the orientation names the three directories and
the gates that judge them.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: the async executor and nish:async readable, writable and sleep
entries.body:
An async task can now wait on the kernel. `await readable(fd)`, `await writable(fd)` and `await sleep(ms)` from `nish:async` park the task on one executor per process (`runtime/runtime-async.c`: epoll on Linux, kqueue on Darwin, a timer heap), and the other tasks and `main` run in the meantime. A wait answers `false` when it cannot be made. A completion that arrives after its task finished is dropped by its generation.

The three debts stage 4 left are paid. Each spawned task allocates in a region of its own, freed when it finishes. A `string` passed to `spawn` is copied into the task's region, and any other non-value argument is refused (NL2673). A `main` that never awaits still runs every spawned task before the program exits. Tasks come from a slab per spawned kind instead of a `malloc` per spawn, and a stuck queue now waits on the kernel instead of trapping.

A program with no `async` function links no executor and writes the same IR as before: 918 of 918 non-async cases are byte for byte. `--emit-ts` lowers `sleep` to `setTimeout` and refuses `readable`/`writable` (NL4017). wasm still refuses `async` (NL2652). The executor's security record is `docs/security/async.md`.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: colour diagnostics on a terminal
entries.body:
A compile error or warning printed to a terminal is now coloured: the location and message are bold, `error:` and `syntax error:` are bold red, the performance, portability and deprecation labels are bold yellow, each `name` the message quotes is bold cyan, the line-number gutter is faint, and the offending span in the source line and its `^~~` caret take the label's colour. The colours are the terminal theme's own sixteen, and a terminal with no colours keeps the bold and faint structure.

The same policy as `--help` decides it (`styleFor(2, agentDriven())` in std/cli.ts): a pipe, a redirect, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb` and an agent get plain text, and `FORCE_COLOR` or `CLICOLOR_FORCE` force colour. `--json` is never coloured. With colour off, every byte is what the compiler printed before, so every `.err` golden is unchanged. Padding and the caret column are computed on the plain text, so the caret still lands under the span after a tab or a non-ASCII character. The style is chosen only when there is something to report, so a clean compile forks nothing extra.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: scan HTTP/1 request heads sixteen bytes at a time
entries.body:
The HTTP/1 parser now finds a line's end with one vector compare per sixteen bytes, in place of the 64-bit SWAR word trick, and scans the request target sixteen bytes at a time with an unsigned range check in place of a byte loop. Parse is the largest per-request stage of Http1Server. On a cold keep-alive connection it falls from ~474 to ~315 ns on aarch64 (NEON), and from ~344 to ~312 ns on x86-64 (SSE2), where the wall-clock ranges overlap and the exact instruction count carries the claim. Accept and reject decisions are unchanged. net_http1_parse_diff runs the new parser against the frozen scalar one over 237,143 cases and catches three mutations of the new scans, and docs/security/http1-codec.md records both predicates, their bounds and those tests.

bench/http1-conn gains a stages shape: 10,000 connections dealt round-robin, so every request lands on a cold connection, with each library stage timed separately (recv, parse, dispatch, respond, sendBody, park). misses.sh adds per-stage callgrind counts, and counters.mjs adds perf stat counts where the machine has a PMU. Its README records the per-stage table on v0.34.1, v0.35.0, main and this change. No std/net stage was above 0.5 µs per request on v0.35.0. It also gives a native timing of the challenge app's Jwt.verify (691–752 ns with SHA-NI), which shows the 2.9 µs cachegrind figure was Valgrind hiding SHA-NI.
metrics: aarch64 perf stat, user instructions per request 8,352 -> 6,812, cycles 3,364 -> 2,818; parse 474.3 (473.7–475.5) -> 314.5 (313.6–316.5) ns, old′ 1.001; x86 callgrind 6,947 -> 6,429 Ir per request

* docs(reference): polish the generated pages, split diagnostics and the spec, group the sidebar

The generated reference pages get one heading scheme (the page title as a
plain H1, an H2 per kind of member, an H3 per member), one icon per kind,

phone's screen, and no grid of a single card.

The diagnostics page becomes an index with a card per band and one page

* docs(reference): break long doc comments up and title every example

A module page shows no paragraph over 120 words now. The std and
runtime/nish.d.ts doc comments are split into shorter paragraphs and
lists, words kept; a paragraph indented one space past the comment's
`* ` carries on the detail or warning before it, so a long one keeps its

They are linked from the pull request at the commit that added them.

A line that opens with "+ " or "- " reads as a list item and broke the

The re-flowed doc comments in `std/threads.ts`, `std/bytes.ts` and

entries.title: the Nish logo and a theme built around it

The docs site carries the Nish logo and a light and dark theme taken

entries.title: async fetch in nish/net/fetch
entries.body:
An async program can now call `await fetch(url)` from `nish/net/fetch`, beside `fetchSync`, and the process keeps serving its other tasks while the request is in flight. A command-line `main` that awaits it simply waits, and `awaitAll(fetch(a), fetch(b))` runs both requests at once. `fetch(url, init: RequestInit | null = null)` answers a `Result<FetchResponse, FetchError>`.

The body is read whole before `fetch` answers, up to `RequestInit.maxBodyBytes` (256 MiB by default, `HTTP_E_BODY_TOO_LARGE` past it), so `res.text()` is a plain method: a method cannot be `async`, and a read body holds no connection. Policy, proxy, redirect and error handling are `fetchSync`'s own, now shared as helpers, so `OutboundPolicy`, `NO_PROXY`, credential stripping on a cross-origin redirect and the `HTTP_E_*` codes behave the same on both paths. Connections can be kept in an opt-in `FetchPool`.

Two differences are recorded in `docs/security/fetch.md`: name lookup still blocks the process (HF-11), and an `https:` URL answers `HTTP_E_TLS` and names `fetchSync`, which serves it. `fetch` does not run under `--emit-ts`.

entries.title: language index cards and pinned citations after the reference split
entries.body:

  certificate_view.cc lines at 62826931 are restored too.

entries.title: module storage, buffer windows and panics a wasm page can read
entries.body:
* feat(interop): module storage, buffer windows and panics a wasm page can read (WP50 stage 3)

First slice: a top-level `const x = new Array<T>(N)` or typed-array `new`
with a compile-time length is module storage. The checker resolves its
pointer-free element and constant length (src/module-storage.ts), and the
emitter lays it out as a zero-filled `@x.data` plus a fixed
`%struct.nish_array` header `@x`, with no initialiser code.

Work in progress: diagnostic codes, tests, wasm-host layout, windows,
panics, the driven bracket, the ring and the page module follow.

Refs: docs/wp50-wasm-host.md#5

* feat(interop): refuse module storage misuse with its own codes

Each refusal of a top-level storage binding gets its own code (NL2671 to
NL2680) and a negative test: an element with a pointer, an enum or range
without a zero, a method that would resize it, binding or passing an
element, for-of, a length not known at compile time, and an annotation
that disagrees with its new. NL2084 now points at module storage.

Refs: docs/wp50-wasm-host.md
Tests: tests/cases/reject_storage_*, tests/cases/storage_module

* feat(interop): a wasm page finds module storage through layout and views

`--emit-dts` writes a `Layout` interface whose lengths, strides and field
offsets are literal types, so a page written for another layout fails tsc.
The loader fills `layout.<name>.at` from the exported `<name>.data` global and
answers `views()`, typed arrays over the current buffer rebuilt only when the
buffer changes. Storage data now has external linkage so the wasm-host link
can export it.

Refs: docs/wp50-wasm-host.md#5-module-storage
Tests: tests/module-storage, tests/cases/storage_module

* feat(interop): report wasm-host panics through a nish.panic import (WIP)

The wasm-host runtime calls nish.panic(kind, site, msg, len, a, b) before
it traps; the emitter tags each panic call with its site and the build
writes <out>.sites.json. The loader formats the message, marks the module
dead, calls onPanic and throws NishPanic; every export runs guarded, in the
arena bracket, and refuses re-entry with NishReentry.

Refs: docs/wp50-wasm-host.md

* test(interop): drive every way a wasm-host module panics from a Node page

The wasm-host-panic section links tests/panic under --profile wasm-host and
checks the panic import, the sites file, NishPanic and the dead module,
NishReentry, an escaping host exception, the arena bracket and out of memory.
The build.sh rewrite now keeps zero-argument panic calls well formed.

Tests: tests/panic

* wip(interop): buffer windows for host imports

* test(interop): a host-window round trip for every element type and both window panics

Tests: tests/host-window

* fix(interop): take a window's element type node from the parser, so it has an id

* fix(interop): give a typed-array window's element its empty type-argument list

* fix(interop): link runtime-wasm.c for a wasm-host panic site and parenthesize a window's offset

WIP: std/host/ring.ts and its test, which still needs module storage to
be lendable.

* wip(interop): lend module storage to typed-array parameters; nish/host/ring and nish/page

Module storage may be passed to a parameter spelled Int32Array,
Float32Array, Float64Array or BigInt64Array, or to a host function's
buffer window: neither can resize or keep it. std/host/ring.ts is a
single-producer ring over an Int32Array; runtime/page.mjs holds the
page half (HostTable, ringOver, reportPanic).

Tests: tests/link/std_host_ring

Reading storage leaves a function readonly, never readnone; writing it
drops readonly; a parallel body may read storage, as the global it is,

Tests: tests/cases/storage_attributes, tests/cases/reject_storage_parallel_write, tests/link/storage_parallel_read

Tests: tests/cases/storage_lend, tests/host-window

`--emit-ts` writes nish-storage.ts beside a program with module storage:

A module storage whose elements are records could ask for more than 4 GiB
and crash the backend; it is now refused at 256 MiB with NL2680, whose

function's first; native IR is unchanged. The TypeScript reading's boolean

The wasm loader now wraps every export in `guarded`, so `twice` is
`(x) => guarded(() => raw.twice(x))`, not `raw.twice`. The negative
checks looked for `name: raw.` and so passed vacuously; they now look
for a `raw.<name>` call, which both forms share.

Tests: tests/run.js simd

* fix(interop): close the module storage and wasm-host review

Answers review round 1 of the stage-3 module storage and wasm-host work.

- A plain wasm program pays nothing. Its loader, `.d.ts` and `.wasm`
  keep main's bytes, pinned by WASM_PLAIN_DIGESTS. The panic guard, the
  `nish.panic` import and the `<out>.sites.json` sidecar apply only to a

- The storage loader's `layout` and `views` names are reserved.
  NL3051 refuses an export that collides with them. NL2684 and NL2685

Tests: tests/cases/reject_storage_loader_name, tests/cases/export_loader_names_no_storage

* style(interop): unnest the loader ternaries

Lint flagged two nested ternaries in the wasm loader and its .d.ts
emitter; both become plain branches, and the touched files are
formatted.

* fix(interop): close the round-2 storage review

Refuse module storage behind a generic interface's implementers, resolve a
lending on in the callee's own module through every import path, keep a
module alive after a bad argument, and give the TypeScript reading the
loader's `views`, `loadSync` and `load`. The loader clears `busy` even when
the arena release traps, the reading's heap is summed in i64, and a build
with no panic sites removes a stale `<out>.sites.json`. The docs state the
panic guard's scope, cross-module lending and the one mutable global.

Tests: tests/cases/reject_storage_*, tests/link/storage_lend_import, tests/panic

* chore(interop): satisfy lint after taking in main

Format the storage and loader sources, replace a nested ternary in the
loader's argument check, write the storage cookbook examples as const
arrows, and keep host-module examples, which must be function
declarations, out of the function-declaration rule.

* fix(checker): recheck storage types after binding; refuse bad loader arguments up front

Module storage of an interface type is checked again once every module is
bound and every generic instantiation drained, so an implementer that only
appears through an import or an instantiation is refused (NL2663) instead of
being laid out as a plain record. Lending an imported storage, by any alias,
is refused as before.

The guarded loader now validates every argument shape before `guarded`
runs: a `Result` must be an object with a boolean `ok` and a payload of its
arm's JavaScript type, read once so a throwing getter is the caller's error,
and an array must pass the %TypedArray% brand getter and is measured by the
length getter, so a Proxy, a re-prototyped DataView or a detached buffer is
a TypeError and the module stays alive. The plain loader is unchanged.

Zero-field interface storage is laid out as a record with no view, and the
TypeScript reading computes offsets in i64. Docs: the module-storage
exception to "a const is not a global", the window check storage always
keeps, the loader's panic kinds and bad-argument behaviour, and where the
TypeScript reading differs from wasm.

Tests: tests/link/reject_storage_import_generic_implementer, tests/link/reject_storage_import_generic_interface, tests/link/storage_import_record, tests/link/reject_storage_lend_import_alias, tests/run.js panic badarg and badshape

* docs(security): re-anchor the wasm-host record and add WH-7, bad loader arguments

The record now cites the lines of the stage's final code, records that a
reporter which calls back in gets NishPanic because the module is already
dead, adds WH-7 (an argument of the wrong shape threw inside the guard and
killed the module, fixed by validating before the call), records storage
values outside their type as open, and widens the index row's scope to the
loader's argument checks, hostImportsOf, layoutLoader and hostWindowProven.

Refs: docs/security/wasm-host.md

* fix(interop): keep an unguarded program's Result loader byte-identical to main

The argument checks a by-value Result got in the previous round reached
every program's loader, so a plain program taking a Result no longer got
main's bytes. The payload writers, resultIn and the loader-local names now
take the guard: a program with no module storage and no host module gets
main's loader, byte for byte, pinned by examples/results.ts in
WASM_PLAIN_DIGESTS. The guide and the security record say what a typed
array over a detached buffer does (copied as length 0), and that a window
of module storage always keeps its bounds check. src/codes.ts is back in
the order gen-diagnostic-codes checks. The security record names the open
storage item WH-8, records the loader hardening left as it is, and its
scope names typedIn, refuse and wasmTypedIn.

Tests: tests/runtime-budgets.js (examples/results.ts)

* docs(interop): date the wasm-host record's line citations to 924c5779

* fix(interop): count WH-8 once, and keep unguarded wasm-host builds off the sites path

The security index counted the open WH-8 as fixed as well; the wasm-host row
is now 0/1/3/3 fixed and the Low total 155. An unguarded --profile wasm-host
build no longer touches <out>.sites.json, and a guarded program whose runtime
is linked only for the panic import exports the arena entry points its loader
calls. The HostTable cost check times 2,000 refused gets, not 200,000 throws.

Tests: tests/run.js page, wasm-size

* fix(checker): renumber the module-storage codes past main's async codes

Main's nish:async work took NL2671 to NL2673, which this branch had given
to three module-storage rules. Those rules are now NL2686 (element kind),
NL2687 (no zero member) and NL2688 (no growing or moving), and the docs
that cite them follow.
